News.title: Newcastle and Liverpool serve up thrilling tribute to Kevin Keegan
News.content:
It is fitting that Newcastle United vs Liverpool is a Premier League opening weekend fixture following the death of Kevin Keegan at the age of 75 last month.

All corners of St James’ Park will pay tribute and show their appreciation for the former player and manager who means a great deal to both sets of supporters.

Fans will find a printed message from the Keegan family on the back of black and white cards on their seat, which they will hold up to display a mural before kick-off.

As well as playing for both clubs, Keegan was Newcastle’s manager when they were beaten by a last-gasp Stan Collymore goal at Anfield in April 1996, a 4-3 defeat remembered as one of the great Premier League games.

This fixture usually delivers entertainment, and with new managers Matthias Jaissle and Andoni Iraola promising front-footed, ‘vertical’ football, there should be goals. That was certainly the case last August, when Newcastle fought back from two down with 10 men, before Rio Ngumoha scored a memorable winner.

It has been a summer of tumult for Newcastle, losing manager Eddie Howe, as well as key players Anthony Gordon, Sandro Tonali and captain Bruno Guimaraes. There has been bullish talk of “Newcastle 2.0” from David Hopkinson, the club’s chief executive, and the club believe they have found a promising coach, but fans have understandably revised expectations downwards.

Liverpool are a difficult team to read; champions only 18 months ago but brittle last season, which resulted in Arne Slot’s dismissal. Iraola’s appointment is a shift back towards Jurgen Klopp’s style. That will be music to the ears of Anfield regulars, but holes remain in the squad. Central midfield has not been replenished; they need a Mohamed Salah replacement, and their strength at full-back is questionable. Much will depend on how 21-year-old central defender Jérémy Jacquet fares alongside Vigin van Dijk but he impressed in pre-season.



Full team news on the way shortly.

News.title: Frustrated Russell fails to make up ground as Norris wins incident-packed Dutch GP
News.content:
George Russell had another frustrating Sunday as the Dutch Grand Prix weekend slipped by with him failing to reduce his deficit to leader Kimi Antonelli. In a thrilling finale to the 72-lap race at the Dutch seaside, Lando Norris took his second victory in a row with two bold overtakes in one lap.

Yet compatriot Russell was irritated by Mercedes team orders for him to let Antonelli through into second place in the closing stages. It was a decision he believed risked a double podium for the team and threatened to put him even further behind his team-mate in the standings, with two charging Ferraris close behind. It was a race that, once again, fell away, despite Russell doing little wrong.

“Is he [Antonelli] fighting for the win or is he planning to catch Norris?” he asked, when the McLaren driver was 11 seconds down the road – the margin he would win by. “Yeah – we just lost a double podium here, mate,” was his response after moving aside.

Whilst Norris, who lost his lead from pole to Antonelli on the first lap, sealed the victory with two superb overtakes on lap 54 – first the Italian and then Lewis Hamilton – Russell had to mount a stout defence from Hamilton to secure third. It was against the odds, as both Ferraris, like Antonelli, were on fresh rubber after pitting under a late virtual safety car. Like Russell, Hamilton was critical of his team for their strategy choices.

Russell’s first podium finish since Silverstone – with his sprint victory on Saturday – means he at least retakes second place in the championship from Hamilton, but trails Antonelli by the same 59 point-gap he had after Hungary. That is despite him looking the faster and more comfortable Mercedes driver on Friday and Saturday.

News.title: Enzo Maresca tinkers his way to nervy Man City win
News.content:
Few in elite sport have the luxury of managing their own endings as Pep Guardiola did at Manchester City, yet no one can ever fully control a beginning. Enzo Maresca’s City started their Premier League season with a win, in the end, but three points masked the scale of the job he faces.

The narrative focus has been the impossibility of filling the personality void Guardiola leaves at a club sculpted in his image. That macro reading overlooks the number of distinct issues with City that Maresca must fix. A new midfield has to be recruited then blooded, a jittery defence needs settling down, and Phil Foden clearly requires help to recover the form which made him Premier League player of the year as recently as 2024.

All of that can wait after this victory against Bournemouth, which quietened some of the alarms from last weekend’s 3-0 defeat by Arsenal in Cardiff. Josko Gvardiol scored an injury-time winner after City had trailed for most of the match, much of it a sloppy slog for the home side, who went behind in the 26th minute. The introduction of Rayan Cherki for Nico O’Reilly revived some familiar attacking effusiveness.

A lesser-spotted VAR-aided double celebration capped a tense but ultimately joyful day for Maresca. Marc Guéhi equalised from Cherki’s well-taken corner in the final minutes, then the expanded Etihad Stadium rapturously celebrated Gvardiol’s apparent winner, only to see it flagged offside. Video assistant Paul Howard intervened to show Gvardiol was onside from Cherki’s pass, before City’s fans, players and staff shouted twice as loud for twice as long to salute a morale-boosting victory.

News.title: How to spend a weekend in Lake Garda
News.content:
Lake Garda’s glittering wind-swept waters have long attracted poets, artists, writers and politicians, from DH Lawrence to Wolfgang Goethe – not least Mussolini, who ran the Italian Socialist Republic from the lakefront town of Salò on the western shore.

Fringed by the Dolomites to the north, Italy’s largest lake is Mediterranean both in feel and in flavour, with a mild, temperate climate and a decidedly slow pace of life. Hills are carpeted in olive trees and vineyards, while citrus groves are thick with plump, juicy lemons. In lakefront villages, restaurant tables spill out onto pretty waterfront squares, while boats zip across glimmering waters.

The lower basin is punctuated with sandy coves and gentle rolling hills, while travelling north, the lake takes on a new appearance, with hills replaced by sheer jagged cliffs that plunge into the waters. The northern shore is swept by mountain winds that create the perfect conditions for watersports, with windsailing, kitesurfing, and flyboarding making this a premier destination for outdoor enthusiasts.

Sports.title: Gary Neville and Jamie Carragher give their Premier League predictions and tip club in Europe to finish BOTTOM
Sports.content:
JAMIE CARRAGHER and Gary Neville have given their predictions for the Premier League season.

And one of them has stunningly predicted a team currently in Europe to finish ROCK BOTTOM at the end of the campaign.



The former rivals-turned-pundits were back at each other’s throats during the first instalment of the 2026/27 edition of Sky Sports’ Monday Night Football.

As has become customary on the first MNF of the season, the panel gave their predictions for the campaign.



Dream Team is back, free, and there’s £100,000 up for grabs!

In years gone by, Carragher and Neville have bickered over who will lift the Premier League trophy at the end of the season.

But this time around, they were united in their belief that Arsenal will retain the Prem for the first time in their history.

Neville said: “One hundred per cent Arsenal.

“They’re way out in front and the squad they have assembled with the signings of [Ezri] Konsa, [Bruno] Guimaraes, [Christos] Tzolis and maybe one more – what a squad they have.”

Carragher said: “A few weeks ago, I thought Man City might have a chance – but it was all around Rodri.

SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

“If Rodri stayed I’d maybe make a case for them, but without Rodri, I just can’t see it.”



Both men had Manchester City and Chelsea finishing in the top four, although their opinions on Liverpool or Manchester United bagging the final Champions League spot, unsurprisingly, differed.

Carragher said: “Man City are better than Chelsea but the European factor can play a huge part.

“We saw Manchester United last season. It gives them a big lift, Chelsea.

“I think Liverpool would want more, but I think just looking at the Chelsea situation, Liverpool where they are right now, I don’t see any way they’d be in the top two, and I don’t see any way they can mount a title challenge.”

Neville said: “Chelsea second? Just purely because of the fact that they’ve got no European football.



“If they keep Enzo Fernandez, with Moises Caicedo in midfield, with that front three, and they’re only playing 45 games, they’re going to amass an enormous amount of points.

“That’s based upon the fact that they’re going to have more free weeks, they’re not going to have the injury pressures.

“They’re not going to have the travelling that comes with European football, and the mental fatigue that comes with that.



“I think they’ll just edge past Manchester City. I can’t separate Man Utd and Liverpool in fourth place, I genuinely have no idea.

“I think City are in a better position than United. At the moment, I’m not convinced by United or Liverpool, but I do think they’ll finish fourth and fifth.”

Carragher had Manchester United and Tottenham finishing fifth and sixth respectively, while Neville had Liverpool and Brighton occupying those spots.

When it came to the relegation battle, Carragher had SUNDERLAND, who will be playing in the Europa League this season, finishing at the bottom of the pile.

He also tipped newly-promoted Ipswich and Hull to go down, while Neville predicted all three of last season’s promoted sides to lose their battles to beat the drop.

Only time will tell if the pair’s predictions will come true.

But one thing’s for sure, they’ll no doubt rib each other at the end of the season if their predictions fall flat on their face.

Sports.title: Jamie O’Hara will be a dad for the 4th time as he reveals wife is pregnant – and has rare birth condition
Sports.content:
JAMIE O’Hara has revealed he will soon become a dad for the fourth time just months after marrying stunning wife Keziah Grubb.

The former Premier League footballer, 39, coined the nickname “Daddy O’Hara” as he made their happy pregnancy news public on Instagram.



While he confessed the couple, who said I Do in April, would be keeping the gender of their first tot together secret, he went on to reveal his stunning spouse Keziah’s hidden health condition.

Alongside an image of their baby scan, the clearly-chuffed TalkSPORT anchor wrote: “Daddy O’Hara is backkkkk can’t wait to make special memories with you, we aren’t finding out the gender but all I know I will love you with all my heart.



“My wife has Uterus didelphys which only 0.3 per cent of women in the world have so it’s a special baby already, only two months left we can’t wait to meet you, you are already kicking us constantly”.

Uterus didelphys is where a woman is born with two uteruses and two cervixes.



According to the World Health Organisation, it affects around one in 3,000 women across the world and occurs when the uterus fails to fuse properly during development in the womb.

Jamie, who is dad to sons Archie, Harry and George with ex wife Danielle Lloyd, was flooded with messages of congratulations from his famous mates.



Former footballer-turned-manager Robbie Keane wrote: “Congrats guys”.

Hollyoaks‘ Gary Lucy quipped: “He shoots … He scores,” before he added the tot would be a “Little Gooner”.

TOWIE‘s Dan Edgar then posted: “Congratulations guys”.

It is the next happy chapter for the ex-Spurs star after the couple’s low key wedding in Kent this spring.

The couple said their vows at St Mary’s Church in Dartford before heading to a modest reception at The Moat in Wrotham.



The couple looked happier than ever as they smiled in the back of a car following their nuptials.

At the time, Jamie penned in his caption: “Mr and Mrs O’Hara I’m so lucky to have the most incredible person in my life forever. What a day”.

Jamie proposed to Keziah last March.

He was previously wed to former Miss England model Danielle Lloyd in 2012.

They had three sons together but divorced in 2014 after the pundit admitted to cheating on her on a night out.

Sports.title: Premier League club leaves fans baffled after asking for new song despite already having famous footie anthem
Sports.content:
CRYSTAL PALACE fans are baffled after their club asked for new pre-match song suggestions – despite having one of the most recognisable tunes around.

The Eagles come out to games at Selhurst Park to iconic banger Glad All Over by Dave Clark Five – but now Palace are looking to mix things up.



A statement from the club is seeking input to try and raise the atmosphere levels in South London yet again.

It says: “Supporters will have noticed a numbers of songs have been played in the final moments before kick-off across the last couple of seasons, including Can’t Help Falling in Love and Insomnia.



“And now, we’re looking for our fans to suggest – and then select – one song to become a tradition moving forward, similar to stadiums up and down the country, to complement the famous Selhurst Park atmosphere.”

And fans online are confused by the call to arms with a 60-year tradition now in doubt.

Glad All Over has been played over the stadium speakers since 1964 after it became a huge hit.

Now heard ringing around the terraces for away fixtures and even when not blaring out over the PA system, it is a matchday staple.

So many can’t get their heads around the need for more change.

One replied on social media simply: “Ummmm Glad All Over?..”



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Another wrote: “I reckon we should go for Glad All Over, by a 1960’s band known as the Dave Clark Five, a bit off the wall I know….”

A third added: “What’s going on here? We already have an anthem, a famous one we’ve used for decades!

“If it’s for a song before glad all over it should be the theme from long Good Friday but don’t change glad all over ffs”.

And a different user chimed in: “Sack whoever was running things last season, just play Glad All Over and next time you have any other ideas keep them.”

Palace lost their opening Premier League clash of the season away to Everton on Saturday.



They will return home with the visit of Manchester City on Friday Night Football.

Sports.title: Jamie Carragher blasts Liverpool’s £445m transfer window last summer as ‘arguably the WORST in Premier League history’
Sports.content:
JAMIE CARRAGHER has sensationally claimed Liverpool might have had the worst transfer window in Premier League history.

Liverpool laboured to a 2-2 draw on the opening day away at Newcastle, with Dominik Szoboszlai scoring an equaliser from the penalty spot with the last kick of the game to rescue a point in Andoni Iraola‘s first game.



However, a number of stars who were backed to have better seasons ended up having particularly poor games against the Magpies.

That included record signings Alexander Isak and Florian Wirtz, as well as full-back duo Milos Kerkez and Jeremie Frimpong, who all arrived at the club in the summer of 2025.



They were joined on the incoming list by goalkeeper Giorgi Mamardashvili, Hugo Ekitike, Giovanni Leoni for a total outlay of £445million in Arne Slot‘s final summer transfer window at the club.

However, with Mamardashvili looking dodgy at best when he does play in Alisson‘s absence and both Ekitike and Leoni missing at the start of this season due to injury, Carragher has not reflected on the window kindly.

Speaking on Sky Sports Monday Night Football, Carragher said: “My fear watching Liverpool, listen its the first game of the season, is this window (2025) could set Liverpool back a year or two.

“Don’t forget, last season it was not about these players. You (Gary Neville) said on the podcast yesterday these players had got off lightly, and you’re right.

“Because it was all about Arne Slot and his style of play, and he’s not like Jurgen Klopp, and he’s holding his players back.

“Yes it’s one game under Iraola, but we’re talking 12 months of underperformance from all of these players except him (Ekitike).



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

“If this doesn’t change in the next two or three months under Iraola and these players improving, I think we’re at that as arguably the worst transfer window in Premier League history.”

After an audible gasp from host Dave Jones, Carragher, 48, added: “In terms of fees for these players and how much and what it was going to do for Liverpool.

“The idea wasn’t just these players coming in and being good players, it was to create a little dynasty for Liverpool.

“Let’s not forget, Liverpool won the league two years ago.



“These [players] were meant to done what [Manchester] City had done a few years ago or [Manchester] United in the past when they go and win two or three leagues in five years.”

The recruits of last season helped the Reds manage a fifth-place finish in the league.

But aside from Ekitike with 17 goals in 45 games across all competitions before his ACL injury, Wirtz, Isak, Frimpong and Kerkez combined for a total of 15 goals.

With the likes of Mohamed Salah departing over this summer, it was hoped the stars recruited last summer would take on the mantle of leading the Reds, yet that is yet to truly materialise.



Liverpool have added defender Jérémy Jacquet and winger Victor Munoz to their ranks this summer, as well as Ronald Aruajo on loan from Barcelona.

Sports.title: Three points from Chelsea’s win over Fulham as Enzo Fernandez CAN have future at club and major transfer message sent
Sports.content:
CHELSEA kicked off their Premier League campaign and the Xabi Alonso era with a 3-2 win at neighbours Fulham.

The exciting trio of Cole Palmer, Joao Pedro and Morgan Rogers were all on display – and all firing.



But Robert Sanchez’s blunders cost the Blues two goals at the other end.

SunSport Chelsea reporter Lloyd Canfield gives his three talking points from Craven Cottage…



CURSE CANCELLED

Chelsea have grown from last season, it seems.

Last season they would have thrown this away and bottled it with a red card in the second half.

They’ve spent money, they’ve got new players, a new manager, a new system, and it seems like things are different this season.

One of those things that has changed is this supposed No9 curse at Stamford Bridge, and Joao Pedro is the man who is putting an end to that.

His opening goal inside 31 seconds was absolutely sublime, and his assist for Cole Palmer was just as good, just as full of quality.

He showed the type of player he is, the type of complete striker he has become since moving to Chelsea.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

And there is clearly no more curse, because he is the one who breaks the spell.

REPLACE ROB & TRUST JOSH

One thing they do need to sort out is Robert Sanchez in goal.

This was a really disappointing display.



Emiliano Martinez is out there – Aston Villa have signed Zion Suzuki. Pay the money!

If you want to be a serious team this season and compete for the title, Chelsea need to get rid of Sanchez and need to sign a serious top-class goalkeeper.

One player who looked like he could compete in this division is Josh Acheampong.

He hasn’t been given too many minutes since he broke through from the Chelsea Cobham academy system – or CNG as it’s now called.

He was brilliant at Fulham.



Among the three defenders, in terms of actually defending, Acheampong was the best of the three.

He’s still young, he can grow into this team, he can develop in this team.

He’s a brilliant young defender who wasn’t given the opportunity to play all that much last season, but I think he should be from now on.



NOT THE ENZ AFTER ALL?

And the last talking point: is there an Enzo Fernandez problem?

He was loudly booed by everyone inside Craven Cottage who wasn’t supporting Chelsea, but cheered by his own fans.

He was okay when he came on, he wasn’t exceptional.

But the reception showed that he can still be accepted at Stamford Bridge.

If he decides he wants to play for Chelsea, that future is still there for him.



What was interesting is that he was benched for Romeo Lavia in the absence of Moises Caicedo.

So it looks like, at this point, Caicedo, Lavia and Reece James are all ahead of him in the midfield pecking order.

That is somewhat concerning.



It’d be interesting to know Alonso’s reasoning – if it’s a personnel thing or if it’s a personal thing between Alonso and Fernandez.

It remains to be seen whether he’ll stay – if he wants to stay – or if that move to Manchester City will happen before the window concludes.

But Chelsea have grown.

A good game, a good win, three goals.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

The most exciting front three in the Premier League, for my money, was on display, and it looks that way going into this season.



But they’ve got issues to fix if they want to be competing at the very top and show just how much they’ve grown.

Sports.title: ‘Did you not watch the game?’ – Cole Palmer in cheeky response to Sky Sports reporter after Chelsea’s win over Fulham
Sports.content:
COLE PALMER gave a cheeky response when he was asked how prepared he is for the season after spearheading Chelsea to all three points against Fulham.

The Blues got Xabi Alonso’s reign off to the perfect start as they notched a 3-2 victory at Craven Cottage.



And Palmer, 24, was the star of the show as he bagged what proved to be the winner in the West London derby.

The Chelsea livewire then showed his comedic side when he showed up for post-match media duties alongside fellow goalscorer Morgan Rogers after the final whistle.



Sky Sports reporter Emma Saunders asked: “How ready are you this season?”

Palmer, who was a shock absentee from England’s 26-man squad for the World Cup, replied: “Did you not watch the game?

“I’m only joking. I’m ready. It was a difficult season with injuries and whatnot.

“But through the summer and since I’ve been back [for pre-season], I’ve worked extra hard.

“Obviously, I worked on the injuries that I had to prevent them happening again. When I work hard day in, day out, I know the talent I’ve got.

“Normally I’m not really an emotional person. I’m not really too bothered about many things in life. But over the summer I was recharged. I’m ready and I’m hungry.”



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

Palmer grabbed an assist as Joao Pedro wrote his name into the history books in the narrow win over Fulham.

The Brazilian notched the quickest goal on the opening matchday of a Premier League season by finding the net inside 31 SECONDS.

Rogers and Palmer were then on target either side of half-time as Chelsea made a winning start to the campaign.

The former Manchester City talent was restricted to just 24 Premier League starts last term.



A recurring groin problem, first suffered in the warm-up before a 5-1 thumping of West Ham, forced Palmer to miss large spells of the campaign.

And it ultimately cost the attacking midfielder a place in England’s star-studded World Cup squad.

Sports.title: Gary Neville and Jamie Carragher make Premier League predictions with shock relegation candidate
Sports.content:
Gary Neville and Jamie Carragher make Premier League predictions with shock relegation candidate

Gary Neville and Jamie Carragher have named their picks for the title, top four and relegation, with the Sky Sports pundits struggling to agree on much after the opening weekend

View 4 Images Gary Neville has disagreed with Jamie Carragher with his choices (Image: Sky Sports)

Gary Neville and Jamie Carragher have given their full predictions for the Premier League season - and while they both agree Arsenal will win the title, there is little consensus elsewhere.

‌



The first weekend of the Premier League campaign has been and gone, with Manchester United and Tottenham suffering heavy defeats at the hands of Hull and Brentford respectively. Arsenal kicked off their title defence with a convincing win over Coventry while Manchester City came from behind to beat Bournemouth.

‌



Liverpool snatched a late point in a 2-2 draw at Newcastle before Chelsea overcame Fulham in an entertaining 3-2 victory on Monday night.

‌



We have now seen every side play and there is now less than a week remaining in the summer transfer window for teams to bolster their squads. It means prediction time for Sky Sports pundits Neville and Carragher, who have opened themselves up to embarrassment by sharing their calls.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

‌



There are no surprises for the title, with both ex-players tipping Arsenal for a second consecutive title. "They're way out in front," according to Neville. But the two cannot agree on the remainder of the top places.

Neville feels that Chelsea's summer recruitment and the arrival of Xabi Alonso can push them up from 10th place last season to second this time around. "Just purely because of the fact that they've got no European football," he explained. "If they keep Enzo Fernandez, with Moises Caicedo in midfield, with that front three, and they're only playing 45 games, they're going to amass an enormous amount of points.

"That's based upon the fact that they're going to have more free weeks, they're not going to have the injury pressures, they're not going to have the travelling that comes with European football, and the mental fatigue that comes with that. I think they'll just edge past Manchester City."

‌



View 4 Images Jamie Carragher has tipped Sunderland for relegation (Image: YouTube/The Overlap)

In typical Carragher-Neville fashion, both is tipping their ex-club to finish about the other's in fourth place. "I can't separate Man Utd and Liverpool in fourth place, I genuinely have no idea," Neville said. "I think City are in a better position than United. At the moment, I'm not convinced by United or Liverpool, but I do think they'll finish fourth and fifth."

Carragher said: "I think Liverpool would want more, but I think just looking at the Chelsea situation, Liverpool where they are right now, I don't see any way they'd be in the top two, and I don't see any way they can mount a title challenge."

‌



At the other end of the table, Carragher has surprisingly tipped Sunderland to get relegated. The Black Cats finished seventh in their first campaign back in the top flight last season to earn a place in the Europa League - and that could cost them.

View 4 Images Arsenal won their first Premier League title in 22 years in May (Image: Getty)

"The fact that they've got European football, they're going to be doing a lot of Thursday-Sunday," Carragher explained. "I think Sunderland last season reminded me a little bit of Sheffield United under Chris Wilder, where they came up and had a really brilliant season, finished high up the table but a lot of the games, like Sunderland, you win by the odd goal. I'm not saying it's luck but their underlying numbers had them not far away from relegation."

‌



Meanwhile, Neville has picked the three promoted sides - Hull, Coventry and Ipswich - to go straight back down, but feels that Fulham under Alvaro Arbeloa could also be in trouble.

Sports.title: Gary Neville 'changes mind' on Man Utd as Jamie Carragher drops Premier League predictions
Sports.content:
Gary Neville 'changes mind' on Man Utd as Jamie Carragher drops Premier League predictions

The start of the Premier League campaign has dropped some surprising results which has resulted in some pundits of note performing U-turns

View 3 Images Jamie Carragher and Gary Neville wasted no time to start jousting their opinions against each other (Image: YouTube/Sky Sports Premier League)

Jamie Carragher has accused Gary Neville of changing his mind on who will have the better campaign between Manchester United and Liverpool just one match into the new season. United endured the worst possible start when they were beaten 2-0 away to newly-promoted Hull City.

‌



Amid the inquisition of what happened at the MKM Stadium, Andoni Iraola's first Premier League match in charge of the Reds saw them seconds away from defeat. His side trailed Newcastle United 2-1 until Dominik Szoboszlai score a 99th minute penalty to secure a 2-2 draw.

‌



Neville claimed he finds it difficult to guess who will do the best out of Liverpool and United, something Carragher, who believes Arsenal will win the title with Manchester City, Chelsea and Liverpool following behind them, called him out on during Sky Sports' Monday Night Football.

‌



JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

When asked to choose between the two Premier League heavyweights, Neville said: " Look, do you want me to be honest? Yes. I can't separate United and Liverpool in fourth place."

Carragher then snapped back: " I've heard you've changed it four times over the weekend. So after United played, he changed it to Liverpool. Liverpool played and he changed it to United."

‌



Neville then replied: " A couple of weeks ago, I had United in third. I didn't have Chelsea where they were, but as you sort of get nearer to the season, you start to look at the squads and you start to think about it.

View 3 Images United were outclassed by Hull City (Image: 2026 Getty Images)

"You think about Chelsea and the fact they've got no European football. That'll give them a big edge. I think City are in a better position than United. Look, at the moment, I'm not convinced by United or Liverpool, really, but I do think they'll finish fourth and fifth."

‌



When told to nail down his prediction, Neville crowned Arsenal as his Premier League champions, with Chelsea finishing as runner-up, ahead of City and United. Arsenal, Chelsea and City all began the new campaign with a victory.

Mikel Arteta's side opened their Premier League title difference with a 2-0 dismantling of Coventry City, while the Blues overcame Fulham 3-2 on Monday night. Enzo Maresca's Premier League debut as Manchester City manager also proved dramatic, with late goals from Marc Guehi and Josko Gvardiol securing a 2-1 win over Bournemouth.

View 3 Images Liverpool were seconds away from defeat (Image: 2026 Robbie Jay Barratt - AMA)

‌



The aforementioned trio are three of nine teams who began the new Premier League campaign with a victory. Up next in the Premier League, Chelsea host Brighton and Hove Albion at Stamford Bridge.

City play on Friday night when they take on Crystal Palace at Selhurst Park, while Arsenal are not in action until Monday when they face Aston Villa at Villa Park.

Sports.title: Gary Neville tells Xabi Alonso the one signing Chelsea must make after Fulham win
Sports.content:
Gary Neville tells Xabi Alonso the one signing Chelsea must make after Fulham win

Chelsea kicked off their Premier League season with a 3-2 win over Fulham on Monday night, but the match revealed a clear weakness that needs addressing in the transfer window

View 2 Images Xabi Alonso started his Chelsea stint with a win (Image: Jacques Feeney/Getty Images)

Chelsea have been told they need to replace Robert Sanchez in the final days of the summer transfer window after the goalkeeper endured a poor start to the season.

‌



The Blues kicked off their Premier League campaign with a 3-2 win over local rivals Fulham on Monday night. But while their new-look attack of Cole Palmer, Morgan Rogers and Joao Pedro sparkled, Sanchez looked like his error-prone self at the other end of the pitch.

‌



He allowed Josh King's effort to beat him at the near post before pushing out another shot into the path of Gonzalo Garcia, who headed in Fulham's second goal.

‌



Sanchez has been at Chelsea since a £20million move from Brighton in 2023 and has made 112 appearances for the club. The 28-year-old Spaniard has managed to hold onto his position as number one goalkeeper in west London, despite Chelsea's prolific dealings in the transfer window.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

That needs to change, according to Jamie Carragher, who has urged Xabi Alonso to bring in a new goalkeeper before the window closes on September 1.

‌



"There were things to really like," he said on Sky Sports. "On paper, that front three is sensational. It really is. It looked it in the game. I think Joao Pedro is fantastic. Rogers' first game, what a start. But when you think of him, Palmer and Pedro - that's as good as anything in the Premier League right now.

"But I do think [there are] concerns defensively. They conceded a couple of goals and you look at the goalkeeper. They have to sort the goalkeeper issue out because it's going to come back to haunt them this season, as it did tonight."

Gary Neville added: "They've added an experience player in centre back, centre midfield and centre forward. I don't know if Emi Martinez is available or not but someone like that needs to come in at Chelsea, because that will undermine everything they do.

‌



View 2 Images Robert Sanchez was arguably at fault for both Fulham goals (Image: AFP / Getty Images)

"The positives for Fulham came from the encouragement Sanchez gave them with the goals. The goals were both mistakes. It's a problem."

Martinez's future at Aston Villa is far from certain after the club signed Japan international Zion Suzuki from Parma for around £30m. Martinez had been linked with a move to Juventus and was left out of the squad for their opening day defeat by Brighton.

‌



"Martinez transmitted to us the possibility to have another challenge in his career," Unai Emery said after the game. "Even last year, he was thinking in case he can have one possibility to change for his challenges.

"He didn't do it last year and he performed fantastic with us. This year, again, he transmitted us the possibility to have another challenge and we decided to sign Suzuki because I think he's a fantastic goalkeeper."

Sports.title: Gabriel Martinelli has Arsenal stars on his side after being pushed out by Mikel Arteta
Sports.content:
Gabriel Martinelli has Arsenal stars on his side after being pushed out by Mikel Arteta

Gabriel Martinelli is poised to leave Arsenal for Saudi Arabian side Al-Hilal after being brutally frozen out of the squad by Mikel Arteta in a controversial manner

View 2 Images Gabriel Martinelli is being forced out by Arsenal (Image: Stuart MacFarlane/Arsenal FC via Getty Images)

Mikel Arteta's harsh treatment of Gabriel Martinelli has reportedly caused some discomfort in the Arsenal dressing room. Martinelli has been frozen out at the start of the 2026/27 season, with the club desperate to sell him before the transfer window closes.

‌



The Brazilian forward has been with the Gunners for seven years, scoring 62 goals in 278 appearances, but appears to have played his last game for the club. He has been left out of the squads for the Community Shield win over Manchester City and the opening-day thrashing of Coventry.

‌



Martinelli has less than a year remaining on his contract and Arsenal have decided now is the time to sell. After rejecting a move to Galatasaray, Martinelli is now poised to join Al-Hilal for a free in the region of £50million, which would be a record sale for Arsenal.

‌



That windfall will help the club sign the world-class forward they have been chasing all summer, with Atletico Madrid striker Julian Alvarez still a possibility. But the way they have pushed Martinelli towards the exit has come at a cost.

FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

‌



ESPN Brazil reports that, unsurprisingly, Martinelli is unhappy at the way in which he's been cast aside in the last few weeks. The 25-year-old reportedly didn't receive a medal for the team's Community Shield triumph and there has been plenty of sympathy from his team-mates.

As Mirror Football have reported, moving on Martinelli, Gabriel Jesus and Fabio Vieira before September 1 has been seen as an important part of Arsenal's summer business. But the way in which Arteta has gone about it has risked triggering a backlash.

Speaking to Sky Sports after the 3-0 win over Coventry on Friday night, club legend Ian Wright said: "With respect to Martinelli and the way he's being treated at the moment, it really makes me uncomfortable.

‌



View 2 Images Gabriel Martinelli didn't receive a medal for the Community Shield win (Image: Stuart MacFarlane/Arsenal FC via Getty Images)

"He always gives 100 per cent, we're not saying he's the greatest, but he's come up with some big moments for Arsenal in big games, and the way he's being treated at the end here – I know they might want him out and there's a lot of guys saying it's time for him to move on, but there's ways of doing that should suit him as well."

Wright added: "For him to be nowhere near it, just makes me feel a bit sad for him. I think he's done enough in this squad to be treated with a bit more respect than he's been treated at the moment."

Article continues below

Martinelli could be about to become Arsenal's record sale, eclipsing the £35m Liverpool paid for midfielder Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain in 2017. He would follow Leandro Trossard, Jakub Kiwior and Christian Norgaard out the door this summer.

Man Utd news: Lewis Hall transfer stance clear as defender ‘in talks’ over future

Manchester United have been linked with several targets in the summer transfer window, including Newcastle defender Lewis Hall

Manchester United are working on strengthening their squad in the final stretch of the summer transfer window. Manager Michael Carrick has already welcomed several new players but will know more recruits are needed after his side’s defeat at the weekend.

‌



Both Youri Tielemans and Andrey Santos started in midfield as the club endured a 2-0 defeat to Hull City. The new signings are set to face fresh competition for their place after United agreed a fee with Brighton for Carlos Baleba.

‌



In defence, Carrick’s side are searching for a left-back to provide competition with Luke Shaw. United have been linked with a move for Newcastle’s Lewis Hall, with his manager making his thoughts clear about the potential move.

‌



Meanwhile, Barcelona’s Alejandro Balde has emerged as an alternative left-back target. Here, Mirror Football looks at some of the biggest stories surrounding United.

Lewis Hall transfer stance clear

Newcastle boss Matthias Jaissle has seemingly ruled out the possibility of Lewis Hall heading to Old Trafford this summer. United have been heavily linked with Hall following the 21-year-old’s impressive displays for the Magpies.

‌



Michael Carrick snaps at reporter for 'ridiculous' Man Utd question after Hull defeat READ MORE :

Legendary goalkeeper Peter Schmeichel brought up the transfer speculation around Hall when meeting Newcastle manager Matthias Jaissle. Hall played against Liverpool on Sunday and earned praise for his performance before conceding a crucial penalty that denied Newcastle the win. Barcelona boss Hansi Flick was reportedly set for talks with Balde on Monday following reports questioning the defender’s future at the club. The 22-year-old has been linked with a move to United and was left out of Barcelona’s matchday squad against Elche on Sunday.

‌



Spanish publication Sport reported that Flick and Balde were scheduled to have a “face-to -face meeting” on Monday after the full-back was dropped for the 5-0 win over Elche. It is claimed that the talks could “open the door” for the defender to leave the Catalan club if the situation cannot be resolved.

The report claims that Flick is willing to keep Balde but wants the player to be determined to force his way back into the team. Meanwhile, Barcelona already have Joao Cancelo, Xavi Espart and Gerard Martin as possible left-back options, if Balde were to leave the Camp Nou.

When asked about his decision to leave the defender out, Flick said: "I spoke with Alejandro Balde today and said to him that I think you're not here 100%, so it's best that you stay at home and clear your mind. We will talk again tomorrow."

Sports.title: Morgan Rogers makes Cole Palmer prediction after Chelsea star's World Cup heartbreak
Sports.content:
Morgan Rogers makes Cole Palmer prediction after Chelsea star's World Cup heartbreak

Morgan Rogers marked his Chelsea debut with a goal and then predicted his best friend and team-mate Cole Palmer would tear up the Premier League this season

View 2 Images Morgan Rogers and Cole Palmer dazzled in Chelsea's win over Fulham (Image: Darren Walsh/Chelsea FC)

Morgan Rogers scored on his Chelsea debut - and then backed close pal Cole Palmer to prove everyone wrong this season.

‌



Palmer scored and provided an assist as Chelsea made a winning start under new boss Xabi Alonso at Craven Cottage. It was a sweet moment for Palmer after his World Cup snub and £117m British record buy Rogers says they are determined to push for major trophies.

‌



Chelsea star Rogers said about Palmer: “Everyone knows how good he is. Obviously, had a difficult year with injuries and stuff last year, and you can see in his eyes in preseason and in training that he's ready this year and he's ready to prove people wrong.

‌



"You saw that with that performance -- best player on the pitch by a mile, and that's what he does. Good to have him on our side."

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

Rogers was also happy with his own debut as he scored for the new-look Blues. Rogers said: “It's nice. You want to settle in as quickly as possible, integrate with the squad and the fans. To feel that affection in the first game and to score is a really nice moment for me.”

‌



Palmer also admitted that he is determined to prove a point this season and is also happy to play with his friend Rogers.

He said: “When you grow up you want to play or do anything with your best friends, so playing football at the best level feels surreal.

“I'm ready you know. It was a difficult season with injuries and whatnot but through the summer and since I've been back I've worked extra hard. Obviously with the injuries I've had to try and prevent them and work extra hard day in, day out.

‌



"I know the talent I've got so I can put in performances like that.

View 2 Images Palmer bagged a goal and an assist at Craven Cottage (Image: Getty Images)

"Normally I'm not an emotional person, the people who know me know I'm not usually bothered about things in life, but over the summer I rested, I recharged and yeah I'm ready and I'm hungry."

‌



Fulham boss Alvaro Arbeloa said: “We are not happy because we lost a game we wanted to win. We did a great game and deserved a little bit more but football is not about what you deserve.

“We have to improve in many things but this is the way we need to play - with character and ambition. It's a new project and time is something we don't have. If we continue to play in that way, we will win a lot of games.”

Sports.title: New-look Chelsea deliver for Xabi Alonso - but familiar issue rears its head in Fulham win
Sports.content:
New-look Chelsea deliver for Xabi Alonso - but familiar issue rears its head in Fulham win

FULHAM 2-3 CHELSEA: Xabi Alonso's side put on a real attacking show in the Spaniard's first game in charge in the Premier League with Cole Palmer, Morgan Rogers and Joao Pedro all on target

View 3 Images Chelsea put Fulham to the sword at Craven Cottage (Image: Darren Walsh/Chelsea FC)

The more things change, the more they stay the same.

‌



Chelsea provided a tantalising glimpse of their potential as Xabi Alonso’s new-look Blues produced a sensational attacking performance. Record buy Morgan Rogers scored on his debut and Chelsea looked the real deal going forward with fellow attackers Joao Pedro and Cole Palmer also on target.

‌



But two howlers from Chelsea's error-prone keeper Robert Sanchez let Fulham back into the contest and it is incredible how a club can spend so much money and yet still not address their most obvious weakness.

‌



Chelsea may yet be the closest challengers to Arsenal’s crown but until they sort themselves out at the back their forwards will have to carry on working overtime.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

The sense of excitement around Xabi Alonso’s new-look Chelsea has completely overshadowed the nerves surrounding Alvaro Arbeloa’s reign at Fulham.

‌



Chelsea have broken the bank again with another raft of big-money deals - including British record signing Morgan Rogers for £117m - and brought in a big-name manager.

By comparison, Fulham equalled their record signing with a £34m move for Gonzalo Garcia who followed Arbeloa from Real Madrid. But Arbeloa feels like a gamble from six months in charge at Real Madrid to succeeding Marco Silva’s five-year reign at Craven Cottage.

The gap between the two clubs is huge - and the last thing Chelsea needed was a head start. But that is exactly what they got. The Blues were ahead after just 31 seconds. Fulham defender Jorge Cuenca’s clearance was headed back by Maxence Lacroix and Cole Palmer provided the clever flick-on.

‌



Joao Pedro went clean through, kept his composure brilliantly and then lifted the ball over Fulham keeper Bernd Leno and into the empty net. Even the Chelsea fans in the away end could hardly believe it.

View 3 Images Morgan Rogers enjoyed a dream debut for Chelsea (Image: Getty Images)

Fulham fans were nervous and you could sense the tension in the air - together with a smattering of boos - when Chelsea threatened to expose the home side’s defensive frailties. Arbeloa’s men very much look like a work in progress at the back.

‌



Chelsea had a let-off when Levi Colwill only got a booking for cynically scything down Oscar Bobb but it did serve to whip up the home fans. This wonderful old stadium creates such a great atmosphere.

It was Fulham teenager Josh King who fed off the energy. King’s low shot beat Chelsea keeper Robert Sanchez at his near post to bring Fulham level after 23 minutes.

It was a horrible moment for the Chelsea keeper. It was an absolute howler. It is incredible that, despite spending so much money, Chelsea have stuck with an error-prone keeper who has let them down on so many occasions.

‌



Chelsea got themselves back in front before the break when two big money buys combined. Chelsea’s £52m defender Lacroix pushed forward, his low cross found Rogers and the record buy drilled home. What an introduction.

View 3 Images Cole Palmer also scored in Chelsea's win (Image: Getty Images)

Chelsea gave themselves a two-goal cushion after the break. Sanchez’s long clearance was flicked on by Rogers, Joao Pedro played in Palmer and the Chelsea forward brilliantly nutmegged Leno at his near post.

‌



It looked as if Chelsea would take charge. But Sanchez struck again. Sanchez could not hold Timothy Castagne’s shot, the ball sprung up and there was Garcia to head home on his debut.

It was game-on. And the noise got even louder when Enzo Fernandez came on to huge boos as the Fulham fans gave the Argentina midfielder pelters as he might just be the most unpopular player in the Premier League.

Sports.title: Gary Neville predicts Chelsea's final position as he issues Premier League title verdict
Sports.content:
Gary Neville predicts Chelsea's final position as he issues Premier League title verdict

Xabi Alonso and Chelsea kicked off their Premier League campaign against Fulham at Craven Cottage

View 2 Images Gary Neville has given his verdict on Chelsea's Premier League title chances (Image: Sky Sports)

Gary Neville believes the work Chelsea have done in the transfer market will see them push for second place this season under Xabi Alonso in his first season in charge. The former Manchester United defender has been impressed by the work they've done in the transfer market, but still feels that Arsenal will win the Premier League title.

‌



The Gunners sent out an emphatic statement with back-to-back 3-0 wins, first over Manchester City in the Community Shield and then over Coventry City in their Premier League opener. Despite missing a number of players through injury and fitness problems, Mikel Arteta's side made light work of the top-flight newcomers on Friday.

‌



City nabbed a late winner against Bournemouth, but Liverpool needed a late penalty to draw with Newcastle United, while Manchester United and Spurs were both beaten by Hull City and Brentford respectively. Alonso and the Blues kick-off their Premier League campaign at Craven Cottage, having brought in Morgan Rogers and Mexence Lacroix in two statement signings to bolster their ranks.

‌



FOLLOW OUR CHELSEA FB PAGE! Latest Blues news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Both players started Chelsea's Premier League curtain raiser against the Cottagers, while Enzo Fernandez, who has been linked with a move to City, had to settle for a place on the bench. Despite the new additions, both Neville and Jamie Carragher feel it's going to take something special to beat Arsenal in the Premier League title race.

Speaking on Monday Night Football ahead of Chelsea's game against Fulham, Neville said: "It's a big ask, with the quality Arsenal have, the strength they have, the confidence.

‌



"But I think Chelsea, looking at the rest of [the contenders], and what Chelsea have done in this transfer window, I think they're in a good place. They could push for second."

View 2 Images Chelsea enter another new era, this time under Xabi Alonso

Fellow pundit Carragher added: "We're looking at Chelsea doing OK on the fact Alonso has come in - it feels they've done really well to get a manager of that calibre, given how poor last season was - and the fact they have no European football, and they've been in the transfer market.

‌



"There's definitely a shift there. They've realised mistakes they've made in the past. Chelsea have got five or six really top players.

"Morgan Rogers and Maxence Lacroix could add to that. They're the two signings I really look at.

"If you add them to those five or six players and they perform well and settle in, that's why we think they could have a really good season."

Sports.title: Leeds and Rangers co-owner York arrested
Sports.content:
Jed York, who owns San Francisco 49ers, was initially charged with engaging in prostitution, but prosecutors amended that to disorderly conduct; York was arrested Sunday morning at a mobile home community in East Palestine, Ohio; He was sentenced to one day in jail for both offences

Leeds and Rangers co-owner Jed York arrested in Ohio and pleads no contest to misdemeanour charges of disorderly conduct and possessing criminal tools

Leeds United and Rangers co-owner Jed York was arrested over the weekend in Ohio and pleaded no contest to misdemeanour charges of disorderly conduct and possessing criminal tools.

Court records show that York, who owns the San Francisco 49ers, was initially charged with engaging in prostitution, but prosecutors amended that to disorderly conduct.

York was charged with possessing criminal tools for using his phone to respond to an undercover online prostitution , according to prosecutors.

York was arrested Sunday morning at a mobile home community in East Palestine, Ohio, near where he was born and raised in Youngstown. He was released after posting a $5,000 bond.

He was sentenced to one day in jail for both offences to be served concurrently and was credited with one day served when he pleaded no contest Monday morning. He was also fined $1,150.

Records also show that York had his cell phone returned to him and that $160 that was seized was to be given to the Mahoning Valley Human Trafficking Task Force as part of the plea agreement. York also completed an online course.

Columbiana County Prosecutor Vito Abruzzino said most of these prostitution cases typically end in plea agreements.

"Each case is looked at individually and for specific facts of the conduct, what evidence the police provide, and input from the arresting officer," he said in an email.

"You also have to factor in criminal history of the defendant, and whether or not they have committed these types of offences in the past, and importantly, what the judges will allow."

The 49ers Enterprises - who are the investment arm of York's San Francisco 49ers - own Leeds United. The Premier League club have declined to comment.

They are also part of the US consortium who acquired a majority shareholding in Rangers last summer. However, York is not listed on the club's list of board members.

When contacted by Sky Sports News, Rangers chose not to comment.

The NFL issued a statement saying the league was aware of the arrest and would review it under the personal conduct policy.

Owners are subject to possible fines or suspensions for violating the personal conduct policy.

Sports.title: Arsenal and Al Hilal make progress on Martinelli deal
Sports.content:
Arsenal and Al Hilal have made progress in the last few days over a deal for Gabriel Martinelli.

Martinelli is seriously considering joining Al Hilal if a deal can be agreed between the clubs.

As an agreement on the fee nears, there is also expected to be a sell-on clause involved to the tune of 20 per cent of any future profit.

Arsenal are looking at potential new forward options themselves before the deadline, with Atletico Madrid's Julian Alvarez still their top target.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports' Sam Blitz takes a closer look at the future of striker Julian Alvarez and where he may end up should he leave Atletico Madrid.

Reports have linked them with Juventus forward Kenan Yildiz, but he has picked up a left foot injury and could face a lengthy spell on the sidelines, according to Sky in Italy.

Sky in Italy are reporting that Juventus' medical staff are looking at various methods to find the best possible solution - but are not ruling out surgery that could rule him out for several weeks.

Martinelli was not named in the Arsenal matchday squad for the Community Shield win over Manchester City or the opening day victory over Coventry.

Analysis: Are Arsenal risking being short at left wing?

Sky Sports' Sam Blitz:

Arsenal started last season with Leandro Trossard and Martinelli as their two main left wing options. Should Martinelli's move to Al Hilal go through, they will start this season with neither of them.

Mikel Arteta's side are undergoing a slight revolution in that left-wing role, with Christos Tzolis set to be the only recognised left winger in the Arsenal squad.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from the Premier League match between Arsenal and Coventry.

The Greek winger has started his career in north London on fire - but with a week of the window to go, Arsenal could risk leaving themselves short on that flank.

Eberechi Eze came on as a left winger in Friday's win over Coventry, so there is cover in a makeshift area. The same applies to Noni Madueke, who has also featured on the left for Arsenal.

But Madueke and Eze both have an important role in providing cover and competition for Bukayo Saka and Martin Odegaard - who both don't have the best injury record. They may be needed elsewhere.

Arsenal's attacking targets are also slimming down. There is still interest in Atletico Madrid's Alvarez but that is far from a guarantee, with the Argentine's heart set on a move to Barcelona.

With Juventus' Yildiz now injured, sporting director Andrea Berta may have to produce a major move in the last week of the window.

Martinelli, meanwhile, departs Arsenal as a cult hero. He is one of three Arsenal players - alongside Saka and Reiss Nelson - who was in the Gunners squad when Arteta first took charge in December 2019.

He remained a popular player despite only scoring one Premier League goal last season - albeit an important one against Manchester City.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Speaking from Arsenal's trophy parade, Gabriel Martinelli says there are 'no words to describe this moment'. Watch the Champions Live From N5 parade live on Arsenal club channels.

His record in the Champions League was much better, scoring six goals in his first seven matches in the competition last season - but consistency and confidence was lacking at the end of the campaign.

And Martinelli may be the player who takes the fall to improve Arsenal's overall transfer business. Any deal involving the Brazilian would surely break Arsenal's sale record - which has stood for nine years since Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain departed for Liverpool in 2017.

Arsenal need to sell better as a football club - does that start right now with the Brazilian?

Wright: Martinelli deserves to be treated with more respect

Former Arsenal striker Ian Wright speaking to Sky Sports:

"The way Martinelli is being treated at the moment, it really makes me feel uncomfortable.

"I know they might want him out, and a lot of people might say, 'yeah, it's time for him to move him on'. But there's ways of doing that and it should suit him as well, how he wants to leave.

"Not being involved in the squad, not being spoken to, he doesn't know what's going on. And yes, I know this - he doesn't know what is happening.

"He's done enough with this squad to be treated with a little bit more respect than he's being treated with at the moment.

"If you bring Vini in, Martinelli can say to himself, 'OK, they've brought him in, they've brought Tzolis in, I might be third [in the pecking order].

"But if you bring Tzolis in and have [Noni] Madueke on the other side, you're thinking to yourself, 'I can still have it with these two, I've got something to offer'. For him to be nowhere near it, it just makes me feel a bit sad for him."

Sports.title: Cameron: It will take someone special to beat me - Mayer's not that
Sports.content:
Chantelle Cameron is aiming for a career-best performance when she takes on Mikaela Mayer in their blockbuster main event unification bout in Birmingham on Saturday.

British world champion Cameron (22-1, 8 KOs) faces American Mayer (22-2, 5 KOs) at the bp pulse LIVE arena in Birmingham on August 29 - live on Sky Sports - with every bout on the MVPW-06 main card pitting a UK fighter against a US opponent.

Cameron maintains Mayer - who holds the WBC and WBA belts - is not "special" enough to threaten her chances of victory.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Mayer says she and Cameron are at the peak of their powers

"I really do believe this is going to be a great performance by me - I think it's going to be my best performance of my career, I really do," Cameron told Sky Sports.

"I feel like everything's gone well and there's no reason for it to fall apart on fight night. When I'm like this, and I've put the work in and my mindset is where I want it to be, nobody's beating me.

"I know that all I have to do is do what I've been doing in the gym. I've done everything.

"I'm heading into fight week in such a good place - confident and knowing that it's going to take someone really good and special to beat me, and I just don't think that's Mikaela.

"When I'm thinking like that and acting that out in the gym and everything else, I just know that I'm not going to be denied the victory."

Sports.title: Chelsea's electric front three edge out Fulham in pulsating MNF opener
Sports.content:
Cole Palmer was back to his best to get Xabi Alonso's Chelsea career off to a winning start in a chaotic 3-2 victory at Fulham on Monday Night Football.

The Blues' attacking trio of Palmer, Joao Pedro and Morgan Rogers looked every bit the most potent in the Premier League as all three scored in a game where entertainment reigned and defending was an afterthought.

Palmer, finally injury-free and all the better for a summer off from England's World Cup campaign, scored one and made another in the kind of performance he had found so difficult to reproduce last season.

If his confidence on the pitch was not evidence enough, his response when Sky Sports asked how ready he was for the new season was emphatic. "Did you not watch the game?"

It took just 31 seconds for him to lay down a marker by teeing up an opener for Joao Pedro - himself refreshed after his surprise Brazil omission. The front three never looked back from there.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Following his side's 3-2 victory over West London rivals Fulham, Chelsea boss Xabi Alonso says he's very happy Cole Palmer is playing with freedom, after the England midfielders' dominant display at Craven Cottage.

Rogers got in on the act on debut with a late run to finish Maxence Lacroix's cross just before half-time, before his flick-on released Joao Pedro to set up Palmer for a third shortly after the break.

Chelsea would have had an easier night despite the surprise absence of Moises Caicedo without a nightmare performance from goalkeeper Robert Sanchez, whose mistakes twice let Fulham back into the game.

The Spaniard, whose position as the Blues' No 1 has long been questioned, let Josh King's powerful but saveable drive in at his near post to level matters midway through the opening period before spilling a shot straight into the path of Goncalo Garcia to allow Fulham to make it 3-2.

The first taste of the Alvaro Arbeloa era suggested the Cottagers will play on the front foot regardless of opposition and they created plenty against their west London rivals - but will need to significantly improve their defensive discipline after being cut wide open for each of Chelsea's goals.

On this evidence they will have score plenty too - and could have snatched a late equaliser when Antonee Robinson horribly miscued a chip with Sanchez in no man's land. But anything less than an away victory would have been harsh on Chelsea, who ran out deserved winners thanks to their electric front three.

Arbeloa: If we play like that, we'll win games

Fulham head coach Alvaro Arbeloa on Sky Sports:

"It's a new project. Time is something we coaches don't have. But if we continue to play in that way, we're going to win a lot of games.

"I'm really happy and proud of my players, what I saw from them. This is the way I want to play. And we're going to play [this way] no matter who is in front of us."

Alonso refuses to criticise Sanchez despite errors

Chelsea head coach Xabi Alonso on Sky Sports:

"It's not about talking about individuals, their situations. It's about understanding what it takes.

"For sure, the first goal we can do better than that. But it's a process. It's day one. And normally it's easier to learn with three points."

The key moments from Craven Cottage

1: GOAL! Lacroix's header from his own half splits Fulham's midfield before Palmer finds Joao Pedro to open the scoring after just 31 seconds.

23: GOAL! King's powerful drive goes through Sanchez at his near post to level for the hosts.

41: GOAL! Rogers' late run to the back post is found by Lacroix's cross and finished off by the record signing, who is left totally unmarked.

49: GOAL! Calvin Bassey needlessly pushes up and is beaten by Rogers to a flick-on towards Joao Pedro, who tees up Palmer to add a third.

54: GOAL! Goncalo Garcia nets his own debut goal as Sanchez pushes Castagne's effort straight at the summer signing.

65: BOO! Enzo Fernandez is met by huge jeers as he replaces Romeo Lavia after his antics for Argentina against England at the World Cup.

78: BIG CHANCE! With Sanchez off his line, Robinson's attempted chip lands well wide in a huge change to equalise.

82: INJURY? Shortly after telling the bench he needs to come off and pulling up mid-dribble, Palmer is replaced by Estevao.

What's next?

Sports.title: Champions? Relegated? One to watch? Carra and Neville's season predictions!
Sports.content:
Jamie Carragher and Gary Neville made their 2026/27 Premier League season predictions on Monday Night Football.

Title winners

Jamie Carragher - Arsenal

A few weeks ago, I thought Man City might have a chance - but it was all around Rodri. If Rodri stayed I'd maybe make a case for them, but without Rodri, I just can't see it.

Gary Neville - Arsenal

One hundred per cent Arsenal. They're way out in front. With what they've got already now in defence and in midfield, with the good attackers that they've got, they've got a really good standard, then they're fine.

Sports.title: Glaring weakness in goal remains but early signs Xabi Alonso’s Chelsea should be fun | Jonathan Wilson
Sports.content:
After a weekend on which pretty much every potential challenger to Arsenal had demonstrated their flaws, there was a sense, perhaps even a need, for Chelsea to emerge as a serious contender – if only to prevent the title race becoming a procession. And while they were far from flawless, there were at least some indications that they could mount some kind of challenge.

They looked extremely dangerous in the final third, and Cole Palmer was involved in all three Chelsea goals, perhaps benefiting from a first summer off in three years. But they were rather less impressive through midfield or at the back, despite Josh Acheampong’s all-action performance, while goalkeeper remains the problem it has been since Thibaut Courtois left.

It could easily have gone wrong: in the final quarter-hour; Antonee Robinson lofted an effort wide with Robert Sánchez off his line and Ryan Sessegnon smacked a shot from a narrow angle straight at the Spanish keeper. But neither opportunity was taken and so Chelsea got Xabi Alonso’s reign off to a winning start.

At this stage, performances and learning the system are probably the most important thing, but if there is to be some sort of dart at the title, results matter if only to keep Chelsea somewhere near the race until the point at which Alonso’s principles are absorbed and they do find something close to top form.

Perhaps what’s most striking, though, is how different the approach is to Enzo Maresca’s. Where Maresca prioritised control to often stultifying effect, Alonso’s game is based on rapid turnovers and transition. It’ll probably settle down as his systems become deeper rooted but there was a sense of recklessness at times to their play. It was harum-scarum, end-to-end, thrilling stuff, which is all very well to watch, and may even come as a relief after the sterility of Maresca and the shambles of Liam Rosenior, but may not be great for consistency or sustained runs of form.

Alonso could hardly have dreamed of a quicker start, João Pedro putting Chelsea ahead after 31 seconds, matching the record for the quickest goal scored in the reign of a Premier League manager, David Unsworth’s goal – also against Fulham – in David Moyes’s first game in charge of Everton in March 2002. João Pedro had scored eight goals in eight pre-season games; and this a player Maresca told not to focus on scoring goals shortly before he went on a run of seven games without a shot. That was a first indication of a forward line starting to show signs of an impressive understanding. All three combined for the third goal, Morgan Rogers flicking on for João Pedro who held the ball up for the overlapping Palmer to slip his shot cleverly between Bernd Leno’s legs.

View image in fullscreen João Pedro (second from left), Cole Palmer (second from right) and Morgan Rogers (right) combined impressively on their first outing as Chelsea’s front three. Photograph: Tom Jenkins/The Guardian

Alonso’s first go at finding a pattern amid the legions of players assembled by BlueCo involved a midfield made up of two players who, despite being at Chelsea together for the past three years, had never previously been paired in the centre: Roméo Lavia and Reece James. It was not entirely by choice: Moisés Caicedo was left out as a precaution while Enzo Fernández remained on the bench until the 65th minute as Manchester City continue their pursuit of him. And it didn’t entirely work. It may look a defensively robust pairing but there were long spells when Fulham had control of midfield.

A feature of Alonso’s approach, and one of the reasons it takes time and commitment to learn – qualities that were notably lacking at Real Madrid – is that players can emerge in unexpected positions. Which doesn’t entirely explain how the right-sided centre-back Maxence Lacroix found himself running on to Palmer’s pass in the Fulham box but, having got there, he demonstrated great poise to skip around Jorge Cuenca and cut the ball back for Rogers to score his first Chelsea goal.

Yet for all that was new and positive, and for all that was raw and unintentionally exciting, there was one glaring and inexplicably familiar failing for Chelsea: in goal. Sánchez’s positioning seemed very strange for Fulham’s first goal, drilled in at his near post by Josh King (who also benefited from a bizarrely ineffectual attempt to track from Rogers), and while it was a far less glaring error, he pushed Timothy Castagne’s shot straight to Gonzalo García for Fulham’s second.

Although Sánchez doesn’t perhaps quite deserve the negative reputation he has among certain Chelsea fans, he did make a league-high five errors leading to goals in 2024-25 and three last season. It remains mystifying that a club that signs wide forwards by the dozen continues to refuse to invest in a top-class goalkeeper. That may yet hold Chelsea back.

Generally, though, Alonso can be satisfied with his start: a win against Chelsea’s local rivals, an impressive display from Acheampong, a number of fluent interactions from his front three and plenty of signs of his system beginning to take hold, with a few obvious improvements to be made. And from the point of view of fans and casual observers, it looks like it should be fun.

Sports.title: ‘Enough is enough’: players pile pressure on under-fire Gianni Infantino to resign
Sports.content:
A group of influential current and former footballers have added to the pressure on Gianni Infantino by calling for change at the top of Fifa, saying “enough is enough” in a statement shared widely across social media.

The intervention is particularly significant given some of those behind its circulation have undertaken ambassadorial activities for Fifa as part of its “Fifa Legends” programme. Among them is the former Manchester United and Arsenal defender Mikaël Silvestre, who also sits on the governing body’s 16-member players’ voice panel designed to assist with anti-racism initiatives.

Others to have shared the statement include the England defender Lucy Bronze, the former England keeper David James and the France 1998 World Cup winner Emmanuel Petit. More signatories are expected to follow in a concerted reaction to Infantino’s ill-fated attempt to sell stakes in the World Cup.

“We share the exact same concerns as the millions of fans around the world,” part of the statement read. “Like them, we have watched the game we love drift away from its core values under Fifa’s current leadership. For too long, we’ve seen major decisions taken without players being consulted or considered, and without any regard for the fans who sustain the sport.

“Change is necessary. Power has blurred the current leadership’s ability to distinguish between its own interests and what is best for football. Recent events have made silence impossible. Enough is enough.”

The group called for efforts to “reshape the future of our sport”, adding: “There are good people within Fifa who want to rebuild trust, but a new era requires a structured change: a real, direct say for players and fans in how football is run. Those who step on to the pitch and those who sit in the stands deserve a genuine voice to help reshape football’s future together.”

Infantino has resisted calls to resign and spent Saturday at a youth tournament in the Dominican Republic, attempting to smooth relations with some of the smaller Caribbean member associations on whose support his fate may hinge.

One former player with a different perspective on Infantino is the former Real Madrid, Barcelona and Chelsea striker Samuel Eto’o, who is president of the Cameroonian football federation. In an interview with CNN, Eto’o said Infantino had not committed any missteps and called for the Fifa Forward Enterprise scheme to be put back on the table if Infantino is re-elected next March. He said the money from FFE would “reset the balance of power” in football and ensure African countries avoided losing top players to other national teams.
